mcat_description.short: Toilet cubicles are prefabricated modular partition systems used to create private toilet stalls in commercial and public washrooms, typically made from HPL compact laminate, stainless steel, FRP, or nylon panels with aluminium or SS hardware.
mcat_description.long: Toilet cubicles are factory-engineered washroom partition systems comprising panels, doors, pilasters, and hardware assembled on-site to create individual toilet stalls in commercial, institutional, and public facilities. The dominant material in the Indian market is HPL (High Pressure Laminate) compact board with a phenolic core, available in 12mm and 18–25mm thicknesses, offering water resistance, anti-bacterial surfaces, fire retardancy, and scratch resistance. Systems are supplied in floor-mounted, ceiling-hung (top-hung), wall-hung, and full-height configurations, with stainless steel (SS 304/316) or aluminium alloy hardware including indicator locks, concealed hinges, and door handles. Key Indian brands include Greenlam Sturdo, Merino, Stylam, Action Tesa, and Galaxy Cubicle India, with products sold per cubicle unit or per project set to architects, interior contractors, facility managers, and institutional procurement teams.

market_context: The Indian toilet cubicle market is dominated by HPL (High Pressure Laminate) compact board systems with a phenolic core, confirmed as the most-in-demand material for commercial washrooms by multiple Indian manufacturers including Greenlam Sturdo, Restloo, Ryka, and CubicleWorlds. Standard panel thicknesses in the Indian market are 12mm (standard commercial) and 18–25mm (heavy-duty/premium), with stainless steel SS 304/316 hardware as the norm. Key Indian brands include Greenlam Sturdo (Greenlam Industries), Merino Industries, Stylam, Action Tesa, and Galaxy Cubicle India. Mounting configurations sold in India include floor-mounted with shoe skirting (preferred for Indian wet-area toilets), ceiling-hung/top-hung, wall-hung/floating, and full-height floor-to-ceiling. Standard Indian cubicle dimensions are approximately 3.5×3.5×7 ft to 4×4×8.6 ft. Buyers are primarily interior contractors, architects, facility managers, and institutional procurement teams; the category is project-driven with custom sizing common. Alternative materials — stainless steel, FRP, nylon/CS panels, and aluminium honeycomb — serve niche segments (premium/hospital-grade for SS; budget/outdoor for FRP; children's facilities for nylon). The category also includes urinal partitions and shower cubicles as adjacent products frequently co-purchased. No BIS/IS standard specific to toilet cubicle partition systems was identified in available sources (single source — low confidence); fire retardancy is typically referenced against EN standards by Indian manufacturers.
